description.p: A raw developer for Linux. It reads the files twenty-nine cameras write, renders them through the camera's own colour profile, and keeps every edit as a list of operations rather than as pixels — so nothing is ever written back over the original.

ul.li: Exposure, contrast, the four tone regions, and a tone curve
Colour balance, a hue/saturation/luminance mixer, and colour grading across shadows, midtones and highlights
Masks: gradients, a brush, a lasso, and regions the photograph is asked to find for itself — sky, subject, greenery
Lens corrections from the camera's own tables, or from lensfun
Crop, straighten, noise reduction and sharpening
A library with ratings and flags, and export in batches

description.p: The Flatpak can reach the network again, for model downloads and the update check, and Numa keeps its icon in the menu after moving from the AppImage.
A menu entry left by a deleted AppImage no longer hides the Flatpak's.

Black and white, AI sharpen, Super Resolution, Remove and Remove people, sensor dust found for you, and exports in AVIF, JPEG XL, DNG, 16-bit TIFF and HDR with a gain map. Photographs in the screen's own colour, two to four side by side in Compare, and hair traced by Refine edge. The first release built as a Flatpak, sharing its libraries and models with any other Numa on the computer.
Renamed from Photo Editor to Numa. A catalog made under the old name moves across on the first run, with its ratings and edits.

Everything a raw developer needs to be one: masks that find what is in the photograph, heal and clone, colour grading, lens corrections for every make, and export in batches. Not 1.0, because it has only ever run on one machine and been pointed at two makes of camera.
